agenda.title: Welcome & Introductions
agenda.description: Who's in the room, why this course exists, and what you'll be able to build by December.
bulletPoints: Course promise: you will ship a working AI agent this semester
Quick intros: name, major, one thing you want AI to do for you

agenda.title: The AI Landscape, September 2026
agenda.description: You picked the wildest possible week to start studying AI — GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 3.8 all shipped in the last eight days.
bulletPoints: Last week's frontier release wave and what it means
The numbers: 91% of businesses use AI, 79% adopting agents — but only 23% scaling them
The adoption-to-scaling gap is where careers are made

agenda.title: Live Demo: A Frontier Model Today
agenda.description: What state-of-the-art actually looks like when you point it at a real business problem.
bulletPoints: From question → research → analysis → deliverable in one conversation
Where it shines, where it stumbles — and why you need to know the difference

agenda.title: Break
agenda.description: Stretch. When we come back, you train a language model.

agenda.title: Hands-On: Train Your Own Tiny LLM
agenda.description: Karpathy-style, from scratch, in free Colab — no experience needed. Build a name-inventing model by counting, then train a real 100K-parameter transformer and watch the quality jump.
bulletPoints: Act 1: a language model made of pure counting (the bigram model)
Play with temperature — the same creativity dial in the real APIs
Act 2: train a miniature GPT live and compare the outputs
Act 3: the scale story — your model vs. GPT-6 is the same objective, 10 million times bigger

agenda.title: Toolkit Setup
agenda.description: Get every account working now so nothing blocks you later.
bulletPoints: Google account + Colab verified (you just used it)
Bookmark Google AI Studio — your API key arrives in Session 3

agenda.title: Course Roadmap, Grading & Final Project Preview
agenda.description: The 13-session arc from talking to AI to shipping your own agent, and how you'll be graded.
bulletPoints: The arc: prompts → APIs → agents → RAG → multi-agent → final project
Final Project: build an agent that solves a real problem — due Wed Dec 9 at 11:59 PM

resources.title: Session 1 Lecture Guide

resources.title: Train Your Own Tiny LLM — Colab Notebook
resources.description: The Session 1 hands-on: build a language model by counting, then train a real 100,000-parameter transformer that invents names. Runs free in your browser, no API keys, ~45 minutes.

resources.title: AI: From Neurons to LLMs (PDF)
resources.description: Background reading that bridges today's tiny model to Session 2: how neural networks scale up into the large language models running the modern AI economy.

resources.title: Karpathy's makemore & nanochat
resources.description: The projects that inspired today's exercise. nanochat is a full ChatGPT-style pipeline you can train for about $100 — the best deep dive on how LLMs really get built.
